# Independent audit of stationary positive-pair descent in a simplex

The completed proof in `candidate 8704554a92158bfc`
passes independent audit. No substantive defect was found. Its conclusion
is a strictly negative feasible second variation, not a claim that every
such critical point has an indefinite Hessian.

## 1. Reciprocal transform and strictness

For a positive log-concave law on the half-line, the survival function
satisfies S(s+t)<=S(s)S(t). Integration over the quadrant gives
E[X^2]<=2(E[X])^2. Equality makes the nonnegative continuous gap zero
everywhere, forcing exponential survival. This proves exactly the
moment inequality needed by the reciprocal-transform calculation.

For A(c)=integral exp(-t/c)h(t)dt, the independently differentiated
second derivative is

    (c/A(c))''=(2M_1^2-M_0M_2)/(c^3 M_0^3).

The sign and all powers of c,M_0 check. Equality at any c makes h a pure
exponential on the whole half-line. Its integrability forces negative
exponent, so the resulting affine reciprocal transform has strictly
positive slope. In all other cases the transform is strictly convex.
Consequently psi(c)>=psi(0+)=1 implies psi'(c)>0 in every case, including
equality in the premise.

## 2. Derivative regularity, including zero other margins

There are at least two strictly positive and one strictly negative
coefficients, which stay away from zero in a sufficiently small parameter
neighborhood. After removing any one differentiated coordinate, at least
two stable nonzero phases remain. Their convolution density is bounded
and continuous, including when the remaining two signs agree. Convolution
with the other phases, including phases whose coefficients tend to zero,
preserves the local uniform bound and continuity. This supplies the
domination and limiting continuity for every first derivative.

When only the two chosen positive coefficients vary, their signs remain
fixed. Conditioning on the negative sum gives two ordinary derivatives
under the integral, dominated by finite exponential moments and bounded
derivatives of its density on the positive half-line. Equivalently the
size-biased densities have four positive phases and continuous first
spatial derivatives. No whole-parameter C^2 assertion at zero coefficients
is required.

The radial exponential change of variables gives
f_V(0)=f_L(0)/d, and shifting all vertex margins gives the gradient sum
f_L(0). Thus stationarity yields P_i=d f_V(0)lambda_i. At zero margins,
size bias changes no V distribution and gives P_i=f_V(0), so stationarity
forces lambda_i=1/d. No boundary coefficient is silently discarded from
the gradient identity.

## 3. Hessian constants and the feasible direction

With f_V fixed when differentiating the auxiliary transform, the exact
entries are

    P_ii=2 f_V(0)phi'(c_i),
    P_ij=f_V(0)(phi(c_i)-phi(c_j))/(c_i-c_j).

At equal positive coefficients the second expression is f_V(0)phi'(c_i).
The factor two appears only on the diagonal and follows from the second
exponential size-bias moment. The convolution ODE verifies the cross-term
sign independently.

Write q_i=phi(c_i)=d lambda_i. The direction with entries
w_i=q_j,w_j=-q_i obeys lambda dot w=0. It is not the trivial radial
normal rescaling, since a negative coefficient outside the pair remains
nonzero and unchanged. The exact quadratic form is

    2 f_V(0)q_i^2q_j^2
       [secant_ij psi-psi'(c_i)-psi'(c_j)].

Convexity bounds the secant by the derivative at the larger argument;
the remaining negative derivative is strictly negative. At equal arguments
the bracket is -psi'(c_i)<0. Hence the cap probability strictly decreases
on this feasible line for small nonzero displacements.

The hypotheses are required only for the two selected positive vertices.
In the full central region every multi-positive proper stationary cap
therefore fails to be a local minimum. The proof does not address
supporting constant-volume traces at boundary points or replace a general
mixed convex body by a simplex.
